dimensions.detail: The name/description (paid enterprise-info lookup) align with the code: the script charges via SkillPay and returns a qcc.com search URL. Asking for payment and returning a link instead of scraping is coherent with the description.

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs running npm install and executing the bundled qichacha.js; the runtime reads OPENCLAW_USER_ID (process.env) for billing. The SKILL.md does not declare OPENCLAW_USER_ID, but reading it is low-risk and understandable for identifying the caller.

dimensions.detail: There is no platform install spec, but SKILL.md tells the user to run npm install in the skill directory. That will write node_modules into the user's ~/.openclaw/skills/qichacha directory. The dependency list includes node-fetch, but the shipped code uses built-in https/http — an unnecessary dependency.

dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The code contains a hard-coded SkillPay API key (SKILLPAY_CONFIG.apiKey) and skillId. The skill declares no required env vars; instead the author's secret lives in the distributed code. This concentrates billing control in the skill bundle (payments go to the embedded key) and is a privacy/trust concern — a more proportionate design would use a platform-managed billing credential or require an environment var so the platform/owner controls receipts.

llm.guidance:
This skill is functionally coherent (it charges via SkillPay and returns a qcc.com search link), but it embeds the author's SkillPay API key inside the shipped code. That means charges are executed using the key bundled with the skill (payments go to whoever controls that key). Before installing, consider: 

- Do you trust the skill author to receive payments? The hard-coded key gives billing control to the author.
- Review the qichacha.js source yourself or require the author to remove the API key and rely on platform-managed billing or an environment variable you control.
- The skill will run npm install in ~/.openclaw/skills/qichacha and install node dependencies (node-fetch listed though not used); inspect installed packages before execution.
- Confirm skillpay.me is the legitimate payment endpoint you expect.

If you don't want external billing controlled by the skill bundle, do not install; ask the author to switch to platform billing or to supply no embedded credentials.
